provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The mechanism is D4-invariant: one full-length horizontal line and one full-length vertical line cross at a single cell. Under any rotation or reflection both lines stay full-length lines, so no axis needs to be specialised. The palette only relabels colours. Background becomes palette[0] and the ring colour becomes palette[4]. The emitted program works in visible coordinates. It finds the row and the column whose cells are all non-background; their intersection is the crossing. It then paints the 8 surrounding cells with palette[4], clipped to the grid bounds, and leaves the crossing cell unchanged. If no full row or column is found against palette[0], it falls back to using the most common colour as background, matching the archived solver.
draft_notes.limitations: This assumes the generator never uses background colour 0 or yellow (4) as a line colour. Yellow is explicitly excluded; colour 0 is assumed excluded by common.random_colors. The generator keeps the crossing off the border, so exactly one full row and one full column exist. If several existed, the first of each would be used. Clipping only matters outside the generator's domain. No fixture contradicts the uniform rule. These are reasoned assumptions; I have not run the factory or the emitted program on the fixtures or on generated pairs.
